# Decompose the `worklist.ts` god class

**File:** `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — 7,823 lines, 89 exported symbols,
20 banner-delimited sections, one 2,260-line function (`runWorklistTui`, 5564–7823).

## Problem statement

`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` carries the entire Herdr work-item selection
experience — constants and maps, the mutable list state machine, row/detail/meta
formatting, tooltip and help rendering, chord and key handling, the mouse input
pipeline, the list renderer, command dispatch and the TUI lifecycle loop — in a
single 7,823-line module. Because the biggest single concern (`runWorklistTui`,
2,260 lines of nested closures over one large mutable context) sits in the same
file as everything else, every change requires holding thousands of unrelated
lines in view, and the blast radius of a diff is not legible from the file it
touches.

This item is the follow-up filed by WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 (producer directive,
intake Q1 → A: *"If any file is >1000 lines it should be evaluated for
refactoring and if appropriate a work item should be created"*). The
downtime-worker decomposition established the pattern this item reuses:
move-only extraction, thin compatibility barrel, tests untouched as the
behaviour gate, sequenced child items.

## Users

- **Herdr UI maintainers (agents and humans)** changing one concern (a key
  binding, the metadata panel, the mouse drag path, the refresh loop) without
  re-reading 7,800 lines.
- **Reviewers/auditors** who need a diff whose blast radius is attributable to
  one module and one test file.
- **Future agents** implementing worklist work items, who need named modules
  locatable by file search instead of a monolith.
- **Operators** who benefit indirectly: smaller modules shorten the review and
  audit cycle for every worklist change.

Example user stories:

- As an agent changing the metadata panel, I want `formatMetadataPanel` and its
  helpers in their own module so that I can verify the change against its own
  tests.
- As a reviewer, I want the key-handling diff to touch only the key-handling
  module so that I can reason about input regressions in isolation.
- As a maintainer, I want every module under 1,000 lines so that any one concern
  is readable in a single pass.
- As a maintainer, I want `runWorklistTui` to be a thin orchestrator over named
  handler modules so that the TUI lifecycle is reviewable.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No production file exceeds 1,000 lines.** After the change, `wc -l` reports
   ≤1,000 for `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (reduced to a thin barrel) and for
   every module created by the split. The single 2,260-line `runWorklistTui`
   function is broken up so no module and no single exported function carries it
   whole.
2. **Public surface preserved — used symbols only.** Every symbol currently
   imported from `./worklist.js` by another module remains exported from that
   exact path with identical types and values, so the 34 importing files
   (2 production consumers + 32 test files, of which 22 are `worklist*.test.ts`
   suites) compile with no import-path edits. 66 distinct symbols are imported
   today; the barrel
   re-exports **only symbols consumers actually use** — unused exports stay
   internal to the extracted modules (inherited producer decision, parent
   WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 intake Q2 → "A, but only re-export symbols that are
   actually used").
3. **Behaviour-preserving, move-only refactor.** No functional or logic change,
   no renames of public symbols, no behavioural diffs. No test file is modified —
   not its import paths, fixtures or assertions — and all 22 `worklist*.test.ts`
   suites (15,433 lines) plus the whole `packages/herdr` suite pass unchanged.
4. **No new circular imports.** Extracted modules import only from concrete
   sibling modules, never from the `worklist.js` barrel or from `index.ts`; the
   existing `worklist → fetcher/visibility/…` edge direction is preserved and no
   new cycle is introduced.
5. **State ownership is explicit and singular.** The mutable
   `WorkItemListState` (848-line section) and the TUI-local mutable context
   currently closed over by `runWorklistTui` each live in exactly one module;
   extraction must not duplicate mutable state or fork the source of truth.
6. **Responsibility documented per module.** Each new module carries a
   module-level doc comment stating its single responsibility, and existing
   provenance comments (work-item ids, section banners such as
   `// ── Mouse / touch input (WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ) ──`) move with their code so
   traceability is preserved.
7. **Testing/validation criterion:** the extracted modules are covered by the
   existing, unmodified `worklist*.test.ts` suites; the split adds no behaviour
   of its own, so no new assertions are required. Validation includes
   `tsc --noEmit`/build success, no new circular-import report, and a line-count
   check asserting every `packages/herdr/src/worklist*.ts` production module is
   ≤1,000 lines.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Relocate code and rewire imports; do not refactor logic,
  improve naming, or "fix" anything encountered on the way (record such findings
  as new work items instead).
- **Barrel compatibility.** 34 files import from `./worklist.js` or
  `./worklist` (including 22 `worklist*.test.ts` suites and the production
  consumers `index.ts` and `fetcher.ts`). The barrel preserves that contract.
- **Sequenced, tree-green landing.** Extract leaf modules first (constants,
  types, layout, formatting) and work inwards towards the state machine and the
  TUI loop, so each merged step leaves the build and the full suite green.
- **`runWorklistTui` is the hard part.** Its 2,260 lines are nested closures
  sharing one large mutable context. The extraction must keep a single context
  object (interface-typed, owned by one module) and pass it explicitly to
  extracted handler functions rather than duplicating state or converting to a
  class-based controller (that would be a behavioural rewrite, not a move).
- **No new runtime dependencies**, no test-file rewrites, no changes to Herdr
  key bindings, shortcuts, rendering output or the `wl` CLI contract.
- **Scope boundary.** This epic targets production modules under
  `packages/herdr/src/worklist*.ts`. Test files exceeding the ceiling
  (`worklist.test.ts` 7,073 lines, `worklist-mouse.test.ts` 1,132 lines) are
  **out of scope** under the recommended option (see Appendix Q1) and would be
  filed as a follow-up item, because splitting them would violate AC3
  (unmodified tests as the behaviour gate).
- **Other >1,000-line herdr files are out of scope** (tracked separately:
  `index.ts` WL-0MVGKGFFN009UCM6, `fetcher.ts` WL-0MVGKH47T007GKN1,
  `dispatcher-anchor.ts` WL-0MVGKHCP9005SJPZ, `downtime-log.ts`
  WL-0MVGKHFT4003X6JW, `downtime-worker.ts` WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7).

## Existing state

`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` is 7,823 lines, 89 exports, 20 sections (line
ranges from the current `dev` checkout):

| # | Section banner | Lines | Size | Exports |
|---|----------------|-------|------|---------|
| — | Header, JSDoc, imports | 1–90 | 90 | — |
| 1 | Input-active predicate (WL-0MTV67MZU003H7SH) | 91–160 | 70 | 2 |
| 2 | Constants | 161–185 | 25 | 3 |
| 3 | `/wl <stage>` argument map | 186–202 | 17 | 1 |
| 4 | `/wl --priority` map | 203–222 | 20 | 2 |
| 5 | Metadata panel sizing | 223–313 | 91 | 4 |
| 6 | Terminal helpers | 314–366 | 53 | 3 |
| 7 | Navigation Stack | 367–443 | 77 | 2 |
| 8 | State (`WorkItemListState`) | 444–1291 | 848 | 5 |
| 9 | Stage filter helper | 1292–1322 | 31 | 1 |
| 10 | Formatting functions | 1323–1618 | 296 | 2 |
| 11 | Hover tooltip rendering | 1619–1855 | 237 | 3 |
| 12 | Compound metadata rows | 1856–1918 | 63 | 1 |
| 13 | Description preview cache / metadata panel | 1919–2456 | 538 | 8 |
| 14 | Note-edit write-back + detail content | 2457–2708 | 252 | 6 |
| 15 | Chord state helpers | 2709–3193 | 485 | 9 |
| 16 | Keyboard handling | 3194–3522 | 329 | 4 |
| 17 | Mouse / touch input (WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ) | 3523–4125 | 603 | 12 |
| 18 | Renderer | 4126–4630 | 505 | 4 |
| 19 | Main TUI loop (commands, dispatch, ship-it, podcast) | 4631–5563 | 933 | 16 |
| 20 | `runWorklistTui` (nested closures) | 5564–7823 | 2,260 | 1 |

Structural facts discovered during intake:

- **66 of 89 exports are imported elsewhere.** Most-imported:
  `runWorklistTui` (21 files), `WorkItemListState` (9), `ANSI` (6),
  `formatItemLine` (5), `handleKeypress` (5), `formatDetailContent` (4),
  `createListRenderer` (4), `formatMetadataPanel` (3), `mapMouseToAction` (3),
  `buildMetaRows` (3). The remaining 23 exports are unused outside the module
  and become internal per AC2.
- **Non-test consumers are only two files:** `index.ts`
  (`runWorklistTui`, `getTermSize`) and `fetcher.ts` (`STAGES`, type `Stage`).
  Everything else importing is a test.
- **`runWorklistTui` internal concerns** (from its nested-function scan):
  pane markers and event subscriptions (5606–6141), metadata blocker resolution
  (5654–5803), refresh/sync/dispatch (6143–6480), key input (6484–7172),
  stdin decode + key-file IO + help entries (7173–7274), render (7275–7504),
  resize + scheduler + hydrator + resume poll (7505–7823). These are the natural
  extraction seams for the loop.
- **Dependency direction:** `worklist.ts` imports from `fetcher`, `visibility`,
  `pane-title`, `events`, `agent-tracker`, `code-freeze`, `ship-guard`,
  `shortcut-config`, `auto-sync`, `scheduler`, `settings`, `db-change`,
  `downtime-worker`, `downtime-log`, `dispatch-view`, `hydrator`, `notify`,
  `command-log`, `form-dialog`, `clipboard`, `ship-it-dialog`, `key-input`,
  `grouping`, `md-viewer`, `md-note-edit` and `@worklog/shared/icons`. Nothing
  outside imports the individual UI internals, so the extracted modules have a
  clean one-way boundary to preserve.
- **Precedent:** WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 (downtime-worker.ts, 8,105 → thin barrel,
  sequenced child items) and WL-0MQJK4UJD0028IRO (`src/database.ts`, 2,584
  lines, completed) used the same AC shape: unchanged public API, tests pass
  unmodified, per-module line ceiling.

## Desired change

Reduce `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` to a thin re-export barrel and move its
contents into cohesive sibling modules, each well under 1,000 lines. The
following decomposition is a **starting point** — boundaries are an
implementation decision, subject to the constraints above and to each extracted
module staying under the ceiling:

| New module | Responsibility | Approx. source |
|---|---|---|
| `worklist.constants.ts` | `SHIP_IT_COMMAND`, `STAGES`/`Stage`, `STAGE_MAP`, `PRIORITY_MAP`, `STAGE_COLORS`, `ANSI`, meta-share bounds, tooltip/mouse tuning constants | 161–222, 314–366, 233–241, 3541–3562 |
| `worklist.types.ts` | Shared exported types/interfaces (`TermSize`, `DisplayRow`, `DisplayHeadingRow`, `ViewMode`, `KeyAction`, `ChordState`, `ParsedMouseEvent`, `MouseClickState`, `MouseDragState`, `MouseAction`, `HelpIconRow`, `NoteEditAction`, `ExecuteResult`, `PodcastTargetResolution`, `ReviewQueueBannerState`, `PodcastNotice`) | types across sections |
| `worklist.layout.ts` | `computeMetadataPanelHeight`, `computeDynamicLayout`, `getTermSize` | 223–313 |
| `worklist.navigation.ts` | `NavigationStackEntry`, `NavigationStack`, `StageFilter` | 367–443, 1292–1322 (~110) |
| `worklist.state.ts` | `isInputActive`, `createGatedTick`, `WorkItemListState`, `isHeadingRow` | 91–160, 444–1291 (~920) |
| `worklist.format.ts` | `formatItemLine`, width/pad helpers, highlight wrap, `formatTimestamp` | 1323–1618 |
| `worklist.tooltip.ts` | `formatTooltipLines`, `formatTooltipOverlay` | 1619–1855 |
| `worklist.meta.ts` | `buildMetaRows`, `pairMetaRows`, description preview cache, metadata panel content/height/format, `resolveMetaLastCommand`, `formatGroupInfoPanel` | 1856–2277 |
| `worklist.detail.ts` | `formatDetailToC`, `formatDetailContent`, `renderFileViewer`, key-file resolution, note-edit write-back | 2278–2708 |
| `worklist.chord.ts` | Chord state helpers, chord hints, footer hints, `HELP_FOOTER_HINT` | 2709–2930, 3176–3193 |
| `worklist.help.ts` | Help-screen layout (`HelpIconRow`, `formatHelpScreen`, wrap helpers, chord help groups) | 2920–3193 |
| `worklist.keys.ts` | `keyToAction`, `handleKeypress` | 3194–3522 |
| `worklist.mouse.ts` | Mouse parse/consume/map/drag/input | 3523–4125 |
| `worklist.render.ts` | `createListRenderer`, downtime status fragment, review-queue banner, row budget | 4126–4630 |
| `worklist.commands.ts` | Command resolution and dispatch: `extractWorkItemIdFromCommand`, `isImplementCommand`, dialogs, ship-guard query, `fetchItemsForView`, `isWlViewCommand`, `resolveDispatchDetail`, `dispatchChordCommand`, `resolvePodcastTarget`, `executeResolvedCommand` | 4631–5563 |
| `worklist.tui-context.ts` | The single mutable TUI context (options, state handles, dispose hooks) shared by the loop handlers | extracted from 5564–7823 |
| `worklist.tui-handlers.ts` | Pane markers/subscriptions, blocker resolution, refresh/sync, disconnect/cleanup | 5564–6470 |
| `worklist.tui-input.ts` | Key input handler, mouse dispatch, stdin decode (`onData`), key-file IO, help-entry builders | 6473–7274 |
| `worklist.tui-render.ts` | `render`, `onResize`, scheduler/hydrator/resume-poll wiring | 7275–7823 |
| `worklist.ts` | Thin barrel re-exporting only the 66 consumed symbols, with a module-layout doc comment | ≤250 |

Where a candidate module would still exceed 1,000 lines (notably the state
machine and the TUI handler group), it is split further along an existing
section or closure-group boundary rather than left oversized.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — reduce to a re-export barrel; preserve every consumed export.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.constants.ts` — new; constants, stage/priority maps, ANSI, tuning bounds.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.types.ts` — new; shared exported types/interfaces.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.layout.ts` — new; layout sizing and terminal size.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.state.ts` — new; list state machine and gated-tick helper.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.navigation.ts` — new; navigation stack and stage filter.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.format.ts` — new; row formatting and width helpers.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.tooltip.ts` — new; hover tooltip rendering.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.meta.ts` — new; metadata rows/panel and preview cache.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.detail.ts` — new; detail view, file viewer, note-edit write-back.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.chord.ts` — new; chord state and hint formatting.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.help.ts` — new; `?` help screen layout.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.keys.ts` — new; key mapping and keypress handling.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.mouse.ts` — new; mouse/touch parse-map-dispatch pipeline.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.render.ts` — new; list renderer and status/banner fragments.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.commands.ts` — new; command resolution, dispatch and dialogs.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.tui-context.ts`, `worklist.tui-handlers.ts`, `worklist.tui-input.ts`, `worklist.tui-render.ts` — new; extracted TUI loop concerns.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — verify unchanged (barrel keeps them compiling as-is).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist*.test.ts` — must remain unmodified; they are the behaviour-preservation gate.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — herdr package overview (worklist behaviour reference).
- `docs/COLOUR-MAPPING.md` — references `worklist.ts` `formatItemLine` and `worklist.test.ts` colour tests; update the file references if module names change.
- `docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md`, `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`, `docs/dev/herdr-events-subscribe-reliability.md`, `docs/dev/pause-when-hidden.md`, `docs/dev/wl-process-spawning-investigation.md` — reference `worklist.ts` by path; verify the references still resolve.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — `runWorklistTui` closure extraction (high).** 2,260 lines of closures
  over shared mutable state; moving them behind an explicit context risks
  behavioural drift in refresh/scheduler/resume-poll ordering. *Mitigation:*
  extract one closure group per child item, keep the context interface-typed and
  single-owner, land each step with the full suite green, and treat
  `worklist*.test.ts` as the gate.
- **Risk — silent re-export drift (medium).** Trimming the barrel to used
  symbols only can break a consumer the search missed (dynamic imports, tests
  using `import *`). *Mitigation:* derive the used-symbol set mechanically from
  the import scan, then verify with `tsc --noEmit` across the package.
- **Risk — cycle formation (medium).** Extracted modules that need shared types
  may reach for `worklist.js` or `index.ts`. *Mitigation:* put shared types in
  `worklist.types.ts` (leaf), and forbid barrel imports from extracted modules
  (AC4), verified by the dependency check.
- **Risk — review fatigue / large diff (medium).** A single big-bang split would
  be unreviewable. *Mitigation:* sequenced child items, leaf-first, one concern
  per child.
- **Risk — scope creep (medium).** The split will surface dead code, duplicated
  helpers and naming oddities. *Mitigation:* record them as new work items;
  do not fix in place.
- **Assumption — test files are out of scope** for the ceiling in this epic
  (Appendix Q1 recommended option A): tests stay unmodified as the behaviour
  gate and the two oversized suites (`worklist.test.ts` 7,073,
  `worklist-mouse.test.ts` 1,132) get a dedicated follow-up item.
- **Assumption — inherited producer decisions** from WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 apply
  unchanged: barrel re-exports used symbols only (Q2), and the epic is delivered
  as sequenced child items in dependency order, one per extracted module (Q3).
- **Assumption — no public API beyond `./worklist.js`** is promised: the
  extracted module paths are internal to `packages/herdr`.

## Related work

- **WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7** — *downtime-worker.ts is a god class* (parent refactor
  series; `discovered-from`). Source of the >1,000-line sweep and of the
  inherited barrel/sequencing decisions.
- **WL-0MQJK4UJD0028IRO** — *Decompose WorklogDatabase god class
  (`src/database.ts`, 2,584 lines)* (completed). Direct precedent: same AC shape
  (public API unchanged, tests pass unmodified, per-module ceiling).
- **WL-0MT2GITCX009WUEW** — *Remove `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` and rewire
  herdr consumers* (completed). Precedent for rewiring herdr consumers and
  verifying the import surface.
- **WL-0MSNULGSM00018I4** — *herdr plugin crashes at startup: Cannot find
  package 'marked'* (completed). Startup-path regression precedent; a broken
  barrel import would fail the same way.
- **WL-0MVGKGMU400631VZ** — *Refactor: decompose `src/sync.ts` god class*
  (open). Sibling item from the same sweep; shares the refactor shape.
- Other siblings from the same sweep (>1,000-line production files):
  WL-0MVGKGHNR0019OLT (`packages/shared/src/database.ts`),
  WL-0MVGKGFFN009UCM6 (`packages/herdr/src/index.ts`),
  WL-0MVGKH47T007GKN1 (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`),
  WL-0MVGKHCP9005SJPZ (`dispatcher-anchor.ts`),
  WL-0MVGKHFT4003X6JW (`downtime-log.ts`).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — herdr feature reference; the module layout must
  stay consistent with the documented behaviour.
- `docs/COLOUR-MAPPING.md` — names `worklist.ts` `formatItemLine` and its tests.

Related work report generated by the `find-related` skill (full report:
`.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B.md`):

### Related work items
- **WL-0MT2GITCX009WUEW** – Remove `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` and rewire herdr consumers (completed)
- **WL-0MSNULGSM00018I4** – herdr plugin crashes at startup: Cannot find package 'marked' (ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND) (completed)

## Follow-up test-file items

Two test suites exceed the 1,000-line ceiling. Per the producer's answer to
intake Q1, they are tracked as separate child items (production modules only in
this epic):

| File | Lines | Item | Type |
|------|-------|------|------|
| `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` | 7,073 | WL-0MVHURHZI000CS5L — *Refactor: decompose `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` (7,073 lines)* | task |
| `packages/herdr/src/worklist-mouse.test.ts` | 1,132 | WL-0MVHUU09608OQSW — *Refactor: decompose `packages/herdr/src/worklist-mouse.test.ts` (1,132 lines)* | task |

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### Q1 (scope — test files) — ANSWERED (producer, 2026-10-21)

**Question:** The ceiling is "no file > 1,000 lines", but the module's test
files also exceed it: `worklist.test.ts` is 7,073 lines and
`worklist-mouse.test.ts` is 1,132 lines. Splitting them would modify test
imports/assertions, contradicting the behaviour-preservation gate (AC3). Should
this epic cover them?

- Options offered: **(A)** production modules only in this epic; tests stay
  unmodified as the behaviour gate and a follow-up item is filed for the two
  oversized suites; (B) include the test split in this epic (accepting test-file
  edits and a much larger diff); (C) include only `worklist.test.ts` here and
  file `worklist-mouse.test.ts` as follow-up.
- **Answer (producer, 2026-10-21): A.**
- Applied: production modules only; two follow-up items are filed for the
  oversized test suites (see "Follow-up test-file items" section below).
- Source: producer reply.

### Q2 (compatibility — barrel) — resolved by inherited decision

**Question:** Should `worklist.ts` stay a public barrel for all 89 exports, or
re-export only what consumers use?

- **Answer (inherited from producer, WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 intake Q2, 2026-10-20):
  "A, but only re-export symbols that are actually used."**
- Applied: AC2 requires the barrel to re-export the 66 consumed symbols only;
  the 23 unused exports stay internal.
- Source: parent item Appendix (interactive producer reply).

### Q3 (delivery shape) — resolved by inherited decision

**Question:** One large change, or an epic decomposed into sequenced child items?

- **Answer (inherited from producer, WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 intake Q3, 2026-10-20): A**

- Applied: this item stays an `epic`; children are created and sequenced at plan

- **Q: How many symbols are consumed externally?** — 66 of 89 exports; 34 files

data.description:
## Problem statement

When the `implement.py finish` test gate fails **without structured test failures**, the operator receives zero diagnostics — an empty `Failures:` message that does not say *why* the gate failed. Three distinct root causes produced the identical empty message during WL-0MVEDM8OT007WDRS, each costing a 20–45 minute blind retry.

## Users

Operators and agents running `/skill:implement` on any repo. On a gate failure they must immediately see the root cause — slot contention, unparsed command output, or genuine test failures — to decide between retrying, waiting for a free slot, or fixing code.

User story: *"As an implement-operator, when the test gate fails, I want the failure message to include the root-cause diagnostic, so I can retry or fix without a blind 20–45 min retry."*

## Acceptance Criteria

- A gate run that fails on slot contention reports the notice text in `phase_finish`'s `message` (and does not look like a code failure).
- A gate run with unparsed vitest failures reports the command's output tail.
- Unit tests cover both paths (guarded result with notices → message includes the notice text; unparsed output → message includes the output tail).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- The full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- `_adapt_guarded_result()`'s result shape is asserted by `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_guard_ownership.py`; changes must remain additive (new keys / non-empty `stdout`/`stderr`), or the asserting tests must be updated deliberately.
- The "no free test slot" classification must match narrowly on the notice text so a genuine test failure is never misclassified as infrastructure contention.
- Risk: matching on the notice string (``test concurrency slot busy:``, sourced from ``TestConcurrencyTimeout`` in ``run_tests.py``) is text-fragile — prefer a stable marker/constant or the exception class over a raw substring, and note any coupling in a code comment.
- Scope: surfacing the reason in the message is in scope. The automatic retry with a longer `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` mentioned in the desired change ("ideally retried automatically") is **optional** — include only if trivial, otherwise record as a follow-up work item rather than expanding scope.

## Existing state

- `_adapt_guarded_result()` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` ~L2644) copies `failures` from the `guarded_run_all` result but **drops `notices`** and hard-codes `stdout=""`/`stderr=""`.
- `phase_finish` (~L4165) builds `Failures:` from `failures[:20]`, else falls back to `test_result["stderr"][:1000]` — empty when there are no failures and no stderr, producing the blank message.
- `run_tests.guarded_run_all` / `run_all` already aggregate `notices` per suite (slot-busy reason, command-not-found, suite timeout); implement.py simply never carries them.

## Desired change

- `_adapt_guarded_result()` carries the guarded run's `notices` and a useful `stderr`/`stdout` excerpt (e.g. the tail of the notice list plus the last N lines of command output) so `phase_finish` reports *why* the gate failed.
- `phase_finish`'s failure message distinguishes "no free test slot" (a retryable infrastructure condition) from genuine test failures, ideally suggesting the longer `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` remedy.
- Regression tests cover the empty-failures path (guarded result with notices → message must include the notice text).

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_adapt_guarded_result()` (~L2644): carry notices + output excerpt; `phase_finish()` test-failure message builder (~L4165): distinguish slot contention.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — reference for the guarded-run result shape: `notices` aggregation in `run_all` (~L1823–1851) and `guarded_run_all` (~L2103); slot-busy notice text from `_test_concurrency_slot` (~L1467).

# Herdr: coalesce the per-refresh `wl` spawns into one consolidated read

## Problem statement

A Herdr default-view refresh runs **five separate `wl` subprocesses per pane per tick**: the four mandatory `wl list` subsets plus the `wl next` browse feed (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`). Per-spawn Node bootstrap now dominates the cost (~66 % of the remaining 0.70 CPU-s/spawn is the bare-node floor), so F10 capped the achievable reduction at ~65 % with five spawns and missed the 60 % target (47.6 % achieved). The remaining lever is **fewer spawns**: one consolidated read per refresh tick.

## Users

- **Herdr pane operator** (producer/agent running several Herdr panes on one worklog): wants a responsive worklist without each pane burning CPU on five `wl` boots per tick.
- **Herdr plugin maintainer**: wants one simple, cacheable read seam instead of five coordinated queries with an in-flight memo.
- **wl CLI maintainer**: wants the consolidated command to reuse the existing DB-query and read-cache machinery, not fork it.

### Example user stories

- As a Herdr pane operator, when 4–5 panes refresh every 30 s against one shared worklog, total CPU consumption should drop to **≤ 0.4× the pre-F4 baseline** so the host stays responsive.
- As a Herdr plugin maintainer, I want `fetcher.ts` to issue **one `wl` read per refresh tick** (one DB open, one cache entry), with the displayed items unchanged.
- As an agent relying on the worklist, I want the **mandatory guarantees** (critical items, blocked items and the review queue always shown) preserved by tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A single `wl` invocation returns every subset the worklist needs — critical, in_review review queue, in-progress roots, blocked roots and the browse feed — as a **dedicated `wl worklist --json` command** (preferred) or an equivalent `--worklist-bundle` mode, sharing **one DB open and one read-cache entry**.
2. `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` issues that single read per default-view refresh tick; the mandatory-subset guarantees (critical always shown, blocked always shown, review queue always shown) are preserved by tests.
3. Measured with `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts` (F10): total CPU-seconds per 30 s cycle with 4 panes drops to **≤ 0.4× the pre-F4 baseline (≤ 63.8 CPU-s)**, ideally ~5× fewer spawns.
4. Cache correctness unchanged: identical JSON for identical DB state, write invalidation still bumps the state counter, and worktree / `--worklog-dir` behaviour is unchanged.
5. Herdr refresh output is unchanged for the same DB state (existing fetcher tests + the spawn-reduction simulation pass).
6. **Testing/validation:** new tests cover the consolidated command's response shape, read-cache hit and write-invalidation, the fetcher's single-spawn path, mandatory-subset guarantees and output parity with the per-subset path.
7. **Documentation:** all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries (notably `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`).
8. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Pure read:** the bundle must not write. `wl next`'s auto re-sort is a write byproduct; the bundle must use `--no-re-sort`-style selection (or reuse the selection logic without the write) so the result is deterministically cacheable.
- **Cache reuse:** register the new invocation with the existing read-cache (`src/read-cache-cli.ts`), keyed by `(worklog-dir, argv)` and fingerprinted by the monotonic state counter; a mid-action write must not cache an unrepresentative payload.
- **Fail-open fallback:** if the consolidated read is unavailable or fails (older `wl`, malformed payload), the fetcher falls back to today's per-subset spawn path with unchanged behaviour.
- **No output change:** the consolidated response must feed the same `extractItems` → `selectWorkItems` → `regroupWorkItems` pipeline so ordering, grouping and audit enrichment are identical.
- **Bounded payload:** the browse feed stays limited by the caller's count; subsets are returned with the same filters (`--root-only` where applicable) so payload growth is bounded and no item duplication is unbounded.
- `--worklog-dir` (module override and per-call) and managed-worktree resolution semantics are unchanged.
- TypeScript/Node stack; match existing style; no new runtime dependency unless unavoidable.

## Existing state

- **fetcher.ts** — `fetchMandatorySubsets()` spawns four `wl list` queries in parallel (critical, review queue, in-progress roots, blocked roots); `fetchNextItems()` spawns `wl next` and calls `fetchMandatorySubsets()`, giving five spawns per default-view refresh. An in-flight fetch memo deduplicates *identical* concurrent reads (which collapses the review-queue state query into the review subset), and `fetchChildrenForItems` / `fetchActionableCount` already read in-process from SQLite via one refresh-scoped connection.
- **Read cache** — `src/read-cache.ts` / `src/read-cache-cli.ts` serve `list`, `next`, `show`, `search` and `status` JSON from a shared on-disk cache keyed by `(worklog-dir, argv)`, fingerprinted by a monotonic per-worklog-dir write counter; writes bump the counter and drop entries. `src/cli.ts` performs the lookup before loading the heavy command graph.
- **CLI commands** — `src/commands/*.ts` register subcommands through `src/plugin-types.ts` / `src/command-registry.ts`; `next.ts` owns the auto re-sort and the selection semantics; `list.ts` owns the filtered list queries.
- **Measurement** — `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts` (F10, 4 panes × 30 s × 5 s tick, sums per-process CPU from spawn records) and `bench/herdr-refresh-perf.ts` (spawn-count/latency per refresh).
- **F10 numbers** — pre-F4 baseline 159.44 CPU-s/cycle, after F4–F7 83.58 CPU-s/cycle (47.6 % reduction), target 63.78; per-spawn 1.329 → 0.697 CPU-s against a ~0.46 CPU-s bare-node floor.

## Desired change

1. Add a consolidated worklist read to the `wl` CLI — preferably a new `wl worklist --json` command — that opens the database **once** and returns the critical, review-queue, in-progress-root, blocked-root and browse-feed subsets in one payload, built from the same query/selection code the individual commands use.
2. Make it a cacheable read invocation (one cache entry, same state-counter fingerprint and write invalidation), so repeat refreshes across panes hit the cache as a single entry.
3. Change `fetcher.ts` so the default-view refresh drives that one read (with the review-queue state and browse feed derived from it) and retains the existing per-subset path as a fail-open fallback.
4. Add coverage: command unit/integration tests, cache hit/invalidation tests, fetcher single-spawn and mandatory-guarantee tests, and an output-parity test against the per-subset path; update the spawn-reduction simulation and the benchmark expectations.
5. Update `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` and any CLI reference docs/comments.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — **new** consolidated read command (or a `--worklist-bundle` mode added to `src/commands/list.ts`)
- `src/command-registry.ts` — register the new command
- `src/read-cache-cli.ts` — add the invocation to `READ_CACHE_COMMANDS` / cacheability checks
- `src/cli.ts` — cache lookup path (expected unchanged; verify the new command is served before the heavy graph)
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — single consolidated read, review-state/browse derivation, fail-open fallback
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `doRefresh` wiring so the bundle replaces the per-subset fan-out
- `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts` — spawn-reduction simulation uses the consolidated invocation
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-*.test.ts` — mandatory-subset, review-queue and output-parity coverage
- `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts` — measurement harness (expects the consolidated query)
- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` — cold-refresh cost section updated

## Related work

- **F10 — WL-0MVFRRS2I000G93J** (completed): measured the <= 60 % shortfall and filed this item with the spawn-count lever. This item is the follow-up implementation of that lever.
- **WL-0MVFNMSRW002FI6B** (completed, outbound dependency): spawn-load epic — transient `wl` process CPU usage.
- **WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG** (completed): cut cold refresh cost — in-process SQLite reads, in-flight fetch memo, batched expanded children. The consolidated read builds on this.
- **WL-0MV6C6SLB005HX7B** (completed): one shared in-process connection per refresh — related "one open per refresh" precedent.
- **WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN** (completed): make Herdr refresh snappy after agent updates — parent of the earlier performance work.
- **Docs:** `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`, `docs/dev/wl-spawn-baseline-2026-10-19.md`, `docs/benchmarks/wal-read-latency-benchmark.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Cache staleness (risk, high):** a single cache entry must never serve stale data across a write. Mitigation: reuse the counter fingerprint, cache only when the counter is unchanged since lookup, and add an explicit write-invalidation test.
- **Re-sort write byproduct (risk, medium):** today's `wl next` runs an auto re-sort (a DB write) on some invocations. The bundle must be a pure read; assumption: `--no-re-sort` selection produces the same displayed order for a stable DB. Verify with an output-parity test; if ordering genuinely differs, resolve the re-sort as a separate, explicitly-documented concern rather than making the bundle a write.
- **Mandatory-subset regression (risk, high):** a bundle that silently drops a subset breaks the always-shown guarantees. Mitigation: tests assert each mandatory subset is present regardless of the browse window.
- **Backwards compatibility (risk, low):** an older `wl` without the new command. Mitigation: fall back to the per-subset spawn path (fail-open).
- **Cross-subset consistency (risk, medium):** the five subsets are read in one process but through separate queries; a write landing mid-bundle could make the subsets disagree. Mitigation: serve all subsets from one DB connection inside a read transaction (or the same store snapshot) so the payload reflects one stable state; at minimum, match today's eventual-consistency behaviour and document it.
- **Payload size (risk, low):** five subsets in one payload. Mitigation: keep the browse feed count-bounded and reuse the existing dedupe/merge pipeline.
- **Scope creep (risk, medium):** further per-spawn startup optimisation (F4–F7) is out of scope. Record additional opportunities as linked work items, not scope.
- **Assumption:** `wl` and the Herdr plugin ship together from this repository, so the fetcher may rely on the new command in the same release; the fallback remains for robustness.

## Verification plan

```sh
# CPU-seconds per 30 s cycle, 4 panes (F10 harness)
npm run benchmark:herdr-refresh -- --json --items 20 --cycle-seconds 30 --tick-seconds 5

# Spawn count and latency for a single default-view refresh
npx tsx bench/herdr-refresh-perf.ts --json
```

- Compare the measured CPU-seconds against the ≤ 63.8 CPU-s target and the pre-F4 baseline quoted above.
- Run the changed-scope and full test suites via `/skill:test`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Was an interview needed for this intake?
  **A (agent, based on repo evidence):** No. The seed context already contains a measured problem, a quantified target, explicit acceptance criteria and a named lever, so the brief was drafted directly from that plus a repo inspection. Source: work item description and F10 comment.
- **Q:** Which command shape should the consolidated read take?
  **A (agent, derived from work item AC):** The AC permits either a `--worklist-bundle` mode or a dedicated command; this brief records a dedicated `wl worklist --json` command as the preferred option (cleaner cache key, no change to `list`/`next` semantics). Source: work item AC 1.
- **Q:** Does the browse feed's auto re-sort write belong in the bundle?
  **A (agent, derived from `src/commands/next.ts`):** The bundle must be a pure read to be deterministically cacheable, so it uses `--no-re-sort`-style selection and the re-sort is treated as a separate concern; output parity is guarded by a test. Recorded as a risk above. Source: `src/commands/next.ts` auto re-sort logic.
- **Q:** Is a fail-open fallback required?
  **A (agent, derived from existing fetcher design):** Yes — the fetcher's existing in-process fast paths all fail open to `wl` spawns; the consolidated read follows the same convention. Source: `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MVFRRS2I000G93J** – Verify >=60% CPU-second reduction per refresh cycle (completed)
- **WL-0MSHJ2NWZ000P3X9** – [test-failure] read-cache spawn reduction (6-pane simulation) cuts work spawns by ≥60% across a simulated 6-pane refresh — failing test (completed)
- **WL-0MVFRR98A008MM19** – Spawn instrumentation: per-process CPU and RSS (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: acceptance, always, bare, baseline, behaviour (+101 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: always, bare, baseline, behaviour, bench (+92 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: achieved, always, bare, behaviour, blocked (+86 more)

# Refactor: decompose `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` (7,073 lines)

**File:** `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — 7,073 lines.

## Problem statement

The worklist test suite is a 7,073-line monolith that covers all worklist
functionality — state, formatting, mouse input, key handling, rendering, TUI
integration, hydration, etc. Navigating and editing one concern requires holding
thousands of unrelated tests in view.

## Goal

Break the test file into cohesive modules so no file exceeds 1,000 lines.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. No file exceeds 1,000 lines.
2. All imports still resolve; all existing tests pass without modification to
   their assertions (move-only refactor).
3. No new circular imports.
4. All related documentation updated; full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Relocate test groups and update imports; do not change test
  assertions or test logic.
- **Test-file scope.** This item exists because the producer declined to include
  test-file decomposition in WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B (intake Q1 → answer A):
  "production modules only; tests stay unmodified as the behaviour gate and a
  follow-up item is filed for the two oversized suites."
- **Sequenced, tree-green landing.** Extract leaf test groups first.

## Related work

- **WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B** — *Decompose packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts god class*
